title: QuasarGPU + Redwood partner discovery
summary: Introductory partner discovery between Redwood and QuasarGPU to explore GPU supply + joint go-to-market for Dedicated/Private inference. Covered compatibility, firmware/driver matrix, performance benchmarks (A100/H100 variants), security requirements (KMS, SOC2), and potential integration touchpoints (OEM images, kernel modules, operator). Agreed on a technical deep dive and a pricing/partner deck follow-up.
topics: performance benchmarking (latency/cost) and KV cache impacts
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Miller: Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick 45 min slot, we want to learn about Quasar's partner motion and surface how Redwood integrates with gpu vendors.
[00:12] Liam Chen: Yeah thanks jordan. Excited to chat. quick intros — im liam partnerships, elena leads solutions, mateo is engineering and sofia product.
[00:22] Jordan Miller: Awesome. priya quick intro?
[00:24] Priya Kapoor: Hey all, priya kapoor, solutions engineer, I work on runtime compatibility, kernels, quant profiles.
[00:30] Sam Ortiz: Sam from partnerships at Redwood, I'll help track next steps.
[00:34] Dr. Elena Varga: Cool. high level — Quasar builds custom GPU boards optimized for high-density inference, we do both OEM and co-lo rack units. We recently shipped an h100-variant and are looking at cert programs with inference platforms.
[00:48] Jordan Miller: Great — typical partner discovery: understand the hardware and firmware surface, integration points (drivers, operator, AMI images), then go-to-market motion. Could you say more about your software stack?
[00:59] Mateo Ruiz: Sure. We run a custom kernel module on top of mainline linux, and offer our own drivers which are slight forks of upstream. We also provide an operator for bare-metal orchestration; many customers run kubernetes but some use metal-as-a-service.
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: Got it — quick question on KV cache and memory model: do you expose low-latency GPU-to-host cache primitives or is it standard cuda/pci-e nic? We ask because Redwood runtime uses KV caching to reduce token work and we instrument memory paths.
[01:30] Mateo Ruiz: It's standard PCIe/NVLink across our variants, but we do have an RDMA option on certain interconnects. we also expose a driver API for pinning buffers.
[01:40] Priya Kapoor: OK that helps. latency characteristics will vary by topology — NVLink clusters will look different than PCIe single node. that's expected.
[01:46] Liam Chen: On the business side, we want to understand how Redwood certs partners and whether there's a co-sell listing. also curious on dedicated offering since our OEMs prefer predictable SLAs.
[01:59] Jordan Miller: Redwood Dedicated is reserved capacity pools with SLA-backed targets. For partner certification we typically do a joint benchmark run + validation on our serving runtime, plus a technical deep dive. On GTM we often do co-marketing and marketplace listings for qualified partners.
[02:14] Dr. Elena Varga: What does the benchmark look like? is it latency p50/p99 across sequence lengths? or throughput?
[02:20] Priya Kapoor: Both. We measure p50/p90/p99 latency across representative prompts and seq lengths, tokens/sec throughput under batching, and cost per token estimates. We also run model quality checks to ensure quantization doesn't regress output.
[02:33] Mateo Ruiz: Speaking of quantization — do you require quantized kernels? customers ask whether 4-bit/8-bit paths are supported.
[02:40] Priya Kapoor: Redwood runtime supports quantized models and we have quant profiles — but kernel support depends on the hardware. part of certification is validating our quant kernels on your firmware. sometimes small kernel tweaks are needed.
[02:52] Sofia Park: On security — we need to know about encryption, KMS, attestation, SOC2. our OEM customers demand kms integration and cryptographic attestation for firmware.
[03:02] Jordan Miller: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and private control plane. For SOC2 we can share our report; for attestation we work with partners on remote attestation flows but that's more involved.
[03:15] Liam Chen: Could we get a copy of the security questionnaire? also curious if you support signed driver bundles or secure boot flows.
[03:22] Jordan Miller: Yes — we'll attach the security pack. We support signed drivers and can discuss secure boot requirements.
[03:28] Mate o Ruiz (mislabelled): [laughs] small transcription glitch
[03:30] Priya Kapoor: On integration options — easiest path is AMI/operator images that include your driver + our runtime. Alternative is to run Redwood runtime as a container with host-driver binding. Both work, tradeoffs on manageability.
[03:43] Mateo Ruiz: For customers with air-gapped deployments, we provide an offline image + firmware bundles. does Redwood have an on-prem packaging model?
[03:50] Jordan Miller: Yes Redwood Private can be deployed in air-gapped environments. we provide an on-prem package and integration guide; some customers want the control plane on-prem while others want a customer-managed network.
[03:59] Dr. Elena Varga: Pricing — our sales folks want to know partner economics. do you have partner margins or reseller terms?
[04:08] Sam Ortiz: We have partner programs; for Dedicated there's typically a reserved capacity contract and channel incentives. we'll share a partner deck that outlines standard terms and referral/commission tiers.
[04:18] Liam Chen: On performance testing, can we run a short POC? we can provide access to 2 racks of h100 variants for a week to run your benchmarks.
[04:26] Priya Kapoor: That would be ideal. we'll want kernel/driver images and a test plan — we usually run a synthetic benchmark plus a few customer-like prompts. also we'll test model variants: fp16, int8, 4-bit quant.
[04:38] Sofia Park: who owns the bench infra? we need NDAs before giving remote access.
[04:42] Jordan Miller: We can sign a partner NDA. also for hands-on work we'll likely have Priya and one of our infra engs run the tests.
[04:50] Mateo Ruiz: timeline-wise we are looking to sign pilot agreements in q1, so a dec/early jan deep dive is good.
[04:58] Jordan Miller: good — sounds aligned. quick notes on common integration gotchas: driver ABI mismatches, cuda/driver mismatch, and kernel module signing. priya do you want to add?
[05:10] Priya Kapoor: yes — also watch out for page pinned memory sizes, OOM under heavy KV cache usage, and scheduler settings that affect latency. if there's a custom operator we need to test pod eviction and preemption behaviors.
[05:24] Dr. Elena Varga: good point. we've seen oom in extreme seq lengths.
[05:28] Jordan Miller: competition question — do you see vendors like nvidia partners/ lambda labs etc? how do Quasar customers compare?
[05:36] Liam Chen: we compete with both — our differentiator is density and firmware optimization for inference workloads. customers who care about power efficiency prefer us.
[05:44] Jordan Miller: ok. On the commercial side, next steps?
[05:46] Sam Ortiz: we'll capture action items. Jordan will send partner security pack and partner deck. Priya will schedule a technical deep dive for kernel/driver compatibility and benchmark plan. Quasar will provision hardware access after NDA.
[05:58] Sofia Park: I'll share our firmware matrix and a short compatibility doc.
[06:02] Jordan Miller: Great. Any final Qs?
[06:05] Dr. Elena Varga: none from us. thanks all.
[06:07] Jordan Miller: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with invites and the partner NDA.
next_steps: Jordan to send partner deck + security pack and partner NDA by 2025-12-19
Priya to schedule technical deep dive (kernel/driver compatibility + benchmark plan) for week of 2025-12-22
Liam to share firmware/driver matrix and provision 2 racks for a 1-week benchmark after NDA

Jordan Miller: Share partner deck, security questionnaire, and NDA; due 2025-12-19
